name: Vertical-specific city-agenda alert digest (e.g. short-term-rental rules)
buyer: Small operators hit by local rule changes, such as short-term rental hosts, small developers, solar installers and liquor-license holders
pain: Agendas are scattered across city portals, run to hundreds of pages, and are posted days before votes.
wedge: Sell one pre-built vertical bundle, such as STR-rule alerts for every Legistar/PrimeGov city in one state, so the buyer sets up no per-city watchlists.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: One shared pipeline over official Legistar/PrimeGov data serves many subscribers of one vertical, so the price per topic can be $15. This price is an estimate.
scan1Edge.falsifier: If City Watch's $19 Advocate tier or an incumbent topic preset already covers the vertical, or buyers will not pay $15, the edge disappears.
scan1Edge.unit: USD per month per topic watchlist

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: The $15/month price and the 80-90% margin are estimates. Costs would be data pulls and summaries. Scraping upkeep for PDF-only towns is not costed.

majorUncertainty: Whether operators will pay $15/month and be reached cold when the category is crowded and a free tier exists.
unknowns: No specific user complaints were found
Full City Watch tier pricing was not confirmed in the excerpt
Willingness to pay for a vertical alert
Scraping maintenance cost for small towns
Whether incumbents will add vertical presets
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Depends on city portals and their APIs (Legistar, PrimeGov). PDF-only towns need fragile scraping. Summaries must link to source documents.
